subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@shoply.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@shoply.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our conversation and proposed next steps so we have alignment. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

What you shared (pain points)
- Heavy reliance on OpenAI for completions and Anthropic for chat; rising monthly spend and unpredictable token costs.
- Latency spikes for peak traffic (cart personalization and search re-rank use-cases) causing measurable page load impacts.
- Need embeddings parity for semantic search and recommendation features (current embedding pipelines tied to OpenAI).
- Compliance/regulatory: want to ensure data residency and audit logs; SOC2 evidence required for pilot.

Current stack details you mentioned
- Inference: OpenAI (completions + function calling for some back-office ops), Anthropic for chat flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings used across search and similarity features.
- Orchestration: in-house microservices on AWS; some workloads already containerized and use internal caching layer.
- Monthly usage estimate: ~120M tokens across products, embeddings ~500k vectors/month.

Success criteria for a migration / pilot
1) Feature parity: function-calling compatibility and streaming responses for chat flows.
2) Embedding parity: vectors with similar retrieval quality (meets current MRR KPIs).
3) Latency: P95 generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts in production-like load.
4) Cost: target 30% reduction in per-token inference cost (or comparable TCO via Dedicated/Private).
5) Security & compliance: SOC2 evidence + region-limited deployment for EU users if needed.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial candidates)
- Llama 2 70B (quantized + Redwood-verified runtimes)
- Falcon-40B / Falcon-7B for chat microservices
- Mistral Large for generation (good performance/cost balance)
- MPT-30B or Mosaic models as embedding candidates (if we need embedding-specific variants)

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to share SOC2 summary and high-level POC SOW (attachments below).
- Schedule 60-minute technical deep dive with Aditya (inference engineer) to validate function-calling and streaming compatibility (can we do Wed Jun 30 or Thu Jul 1?).
- Redwood to provide a 2-week pilot plan and cost estimate for a Dedicated pool + canary rollout.

Attachments: 20260625-shoply-discovery-notes.pdf (notes from call).

Thanks — want to keep momentum here. Please confirm the success criteria above and what else we should include in the PoC scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side:
- Function calling parity is critical for several of our orchestration flows (we use structured function calls with typed arguments today).
- Streaming is required for the chat UX — we need token-by-token streaming in the pilot.
- Embedding quality is make-or-break for our search/recommendation features; we’ll need to run A/B tests against existing OpenAI embeddings.
- Latency target: P95 <= 200ms for the short personalization prompts (we can share example payloads in the deep-dive).
- Cost: our finance team wants to see realistic 6-month TCO scenarios vs current spend.
- Compliance: can you send SOC2 summary and an export of the audit-log format you provide? Data residency (US/EU) is a plus.

We’re available for the technical deep-dive on Wed Jun 30 (10:00–11:00 PT) — would like Aditya on that call.

Thanks — Alex

Alex / Priya —

Great — confirmed Wed Jun 30 10:00–11:00 PT for the technical deep-dive with Aditya.

Per your requests I attached the following for initial review:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level SOC2 scope and what we redact for external sharing)
- redwood-poc-sow.pdf (proposed 2-week pilot scope, objectives, and exit criteria)

Quick notes on the pilot and what we’ll validate:
- Function calling: Aditya will validate structured function call compatibility and identify any mapping work for your typed args.
- Streaming: we’ll demonstrate token streaming in our hosted environment and measure end-to-end UX latency.
- Embeddings: we’ll run an A/B embedding comparison; we recommend starting with MPT-2X or Llama-2-derived embedding variants depending on quality tradeoffs.
- Canary plan: 1) test in Redwood Dedicated sandbox with a mirror of production traffic; 2) run offline embedding A/B tests; 3) evaluate production canary at 5–10% traffic.

Action items
- Shoply: confirm the sample payloads for latency testing and the embedding evaluation dataset (Priya to share by EOD Mon).
- Redwood: share SOC2 summary + PoC SOW (attached) and a preliminary cost estimate for a Dedicated pilot by EOD Mon.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-poc-sow.pdf

Best,
Marissa
